list.label: getting brighter
list.meaning: likely drier, rougher or freshly bare ground

narrative.t: Between 30 Jun 2026 and 28 Oct 2026 (NISAR, 10 passes, track 059 ascending), the main dark body (likely the lake, reservoir or river) grew from 86.8 km² on 30 Jun to 106 km² on 28 Oct, mostly between 24 Jul and 28 Oct (all water-dark pixels in the box: 216 → 219 km²).
narrative.s: Water-dark = smoothed brightness below 84 of 255 (Otsu split in the 30 Jun histogram); main body = largest connected dark patch, 114 km² at its widest

narrative.t: On the map, 41.8 km² that was water-dark on 30 Jun no longer is by 28 Oct (orange, "water lost": drying shore), and 46.5 km² became water-dark (blue, "water gained").
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 30 Jun vs 28 Oct 2026; same water threshold, first vs last pass, only within 300 m of the dark water bodies

narrative.t: Across the whole box, 0.00 km² became much darker in radar (new water, wetter or smoother ground) and 0.00 km² became much brighter (rougher or bare ground, structures, debris or crops).
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 30 Jun vs 28 Oct 2026; more than 4 robust σ (113 of 255 levels) after 5×5 smoothing

narrative.t: The largest single patch (marker 1) is 16.2 km² of water lost, around 69.198° N, 49.483° W (brightness 68 → 105 of 255).
96.1 km² jumped by more than 4× its own normal pass-to-pass wobble, most of it (24.7 km²) between 12 Jul and 24 Jul; the same test on the first pair flags 22.7 km², a rough false-alarm level.
narrative.s: Per-pixel temporal anomaly over 10 passes (median absolute successive difference)

narrative.t: The plant signal (HV-like green channel) rose by 9% across the box, consistent with more vegetation or rougher surfaces.
Grouping pixels that behave alike over time gives 6 zones; the biggest changing one, "getting brighter" (likely drier, rougher or freshly bare ground), covers 138 km².
narrative.s: Unsupervised k-means on per-pixel time profiles; labels are interpretations

narrative.t: NASA EONET lists no natural events; USGS lists no M4+ earthquakes within about 50 km of this box in this period. That is context, not proof of cause.
narrative.s: NASA EONET v3 and USGS FDSN event APIs, box ± 0.5°
